reason: The objective is a structure-to-property mapping that the learner must compare across three groups and re-read, not a process that unfolds in time. Nothing about polarity, hydrogen bonding or acidity is visible as motion, so an animation would add decoration while risking two errors the case explicitly forbids: implying a reaction mechanism and implying that the highlighted group is the whole molecule. The hard parts here are locating the group inside a carbon skeleton and keeping three property axes separate, and both are better served by a labelled figure plus a matrix the learner can scan back and forth at their own pace.
staticAlternative: A one-page annotated worksheet. Top: three skeletal structures (ethanol, propanone, ethanoic acid) drawn at the same scale, with the functional group enclosed in a dark callout box and a magnified inset naming the atoms; a caption states that the box is the reactive part, not the molecule. Middle: a three-column property matrix with rows for polarity, hydrogen-bond donor, hydrogen-bond acceptor and acid strength, filled qualitatively as none, weak, strong with the reason in words next to each cell, and a column recording what stays the same across all three (the carbon skeleton). Bottom: a predict-then-check task, 'Rank these three by boiling point and by solubility in water, then justify each ranking from the matrix', with an answer key that quotes the matrix rather than a mechanism. A final item shows the same OH group attached to two different skeletons and asks which properties travel with the group and which travel with the skeleton.
